`repos` maps a local checkout directory name to a public project/lab slug.
It is the collector's privacy funnel: a directory with no entry here is
counted in the day's totals and attributed to nothing, because its name is a
private repo name and ADR 008 says those never leave the machine.
That is also why the real file is NOT committed. The left-hand side of every
entry is a private repository's directory name, and `coreybain/personal-site`
is a public repository — committing the mapping would publish exactly the
inventory the funnel exists to withhold. The `dir` values below are invented
placeholders; replace them with the real ones on this machine, which
`bun run inventory` will print to your terminal and nowhere else.
Matching is segment-wise containment, longest match first, so one entry covers
the repo root, packages inside it and agent worktrees cut from it.

repos.note: This monorepo — a public repo, so its directory name is safe to commit. Lab `home` is coreybaines.com.
